review_independence.method: Both stored branches replayed legally from the FEN; signed material accounting from the side to move at the root; static exchange evaluation at the stored horizon; and a material-only alpha-beta with quiescence continued past the stored horizon to expose recaptures and forks that four plies hide. Verdicts were spot-checked by hand against the board. No detector implementation, packet builder, answer key, or validation snapshot was read.

raw_blinded_score.recall_warning: Controls are sampled positive-edge near-controls, not an opportunity-denominator population; packet_positive_capture is not population recall.

raw_disagreements.review_note: Qh5+: queen takes knight on d5; pawn takes queen on d5, +3 within the stored line and +3 once every recapture and follow-up past the horizon is resolved.
Qxd6 leaves material at +0 through the stored line (settled +0). It avoids the loss taken in the played branch but establishes no positive target/line payoff of its own.

Nxd5 reads as +9 inside the four stored plies (knight takes knight on d5; queen takes queen on a5), but the line stops before the refutation: past the stored horizon the opponent recovers the material and the balance settles at +0. No payoff is proved.

Qg4 reads as +1 inside the four stored plies (queen takes knight on h4; bishop takes pawn on g2), but the line stops before the refutation: past the stored horizon the opponent recovers the material and the balance settles at -2. No payoff is proved.

Qh5+: knight takes pawn on g6; queen takes queen on c5, +10 within the stored line and +6 once every recapture and follow-up past the horizon is resolved. The stored line overstates the size -- +10 in-line versus +6 settled -- but the gain itself survives.

Bg3 ends with the capture on e1 still recapturable, so the stored line stops mid-exchange. Its apparent +4 reduces to +1 once the exchange resolves; a one-pawn margin that depends entirely on moves the stored line does not contain is not proved by this evidence.
